title: 宿新市徐公店·其二
titlePy: Sù Xīnshì Xú Gōng Diàn · Qí Èr
titleEn: Staying at Mr Xu’s Inn in Xinshi (No. 2)
author: 杨万里
intro: Late spring in the countryside: a child chases a yellow butterfly as fast as he can — and it vanishes into a field of yellow rape flowers. A tiny, funny moment caught forever.
analysis: 这首诗写诗人住在新市一家姓徐的小客店时看到的晚春景色。前两句写景：稀稀落落的篱笆旁，一条小路伸向远处；树上的花已经落了，新长出的叶子还不多，没有形成树荫。这是春末夏初的样子。后两句写人：一个小孩飞快地奔跑，追一只黄色的蝴蝶；蝴蝶一下子飞进了金黄的油菜花地里，黄蝴蝶和黄菜花分不清，孩子再也找不到它了。诗人没有写孩子的表情，但我们能想象他站在花地边东张西望的样子，又着急又好玩。这种从生活里抓住一个小镜头的写法，正是杨万里诗的特点：新鲜、活泼，像随手拍下的照片。最后一句的“黄”和“黄”混在一起，是全诗最妙的地方。
analysisEn: Yang Wanli wrote this while staying at a small inn kept by a Mr Xu in the town of Xinshi. The first two lines set the scene in late spring: a thin, gappy bamboo fence, a narrow path running deep into the distance, and trees whose blossoms have fallen but whose new leaves are still too few to give shade. It is that in-between moment when spring is ending and summer hasn’t quite begun. The last two lines bring in a child. He runs as fast as he can after a yellow butterfly — and the butterfly flies straight into a field of yellow rape flowers. Yellow on yellow: it is simply gone, and the child cannot find it anywhere. The poet doesn’t describe the boy’s face, but we can picture him standing at the edge of the field, looking this way and that, puzzled and a little cross. Catching one small, real moment like this, as if with a quick snapshot, is what Yang Wanli is famous for. The cleverest touch is the colour: the butterfly disappears because it matches the flowers exactly, so the poem ends with the whole field glowing gold.
background: Yang Wanli (1127–1206), one of the great poets of the Southern Song, loved writing about small scenes of nature and daily life in plain, lively language. He wrote two poems at Mr Xu’s inn in Xinshi on a journey in spring; this second one is the famous one.
pronunciation: 一径 yī jìng（小路）；未成阴 wèi chéng yīn。无特殊多音字。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材文本。第二句有的版本作“树头花落未成阴”，统编教材作“树头新绿未成阴”。原题共两首，这是第二首。

lines.py: lí luò shū shū yī jìng shēn
lines.lit: The fence is sparse; a single path runs deep;
lines.en: Past a gappy fence, a narrow path runs far away;

lines.py: shù tóu xīn lǜ wèi chéng yīn
lines.lit: on the treetops, new green, not yet making shade.
lines.en: the new leaves on the trees are too few for shade.

lines.py: ér tóng jí zǒu zhuī huáng dié
lines.lit: A child runs fast, chasing a yellow butterfly;
lines.en: A child dashes after a yellow butterfly —

lines.py: fēi rù cài huā wú chù xún
lines.lit: it flies into the rape flowers — nowhere to be found.
lines.en: it flies into the yellow rape flowers and is nowhere to be found.

words.note: 径：小路，今天“路径”“捷径”的“径”。
古义：“走”是跑，和今天的“走”不同。
这里指油菜花，春天开成一大片金黄色。
寻：找。今天“寻找”“寻人启事”。

imagery.name: 蝶
imagery.zh: 黄蝴蝶是孩子追逐的目标，飞进菜花后就“消失”了，写出童趣。
imagery.en: The yellow butterfly is the child’s prize — and it “vanishes” into the flowers, a funny moment of childhood.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 一大片金黄的油菜花把蝴蝶藏起来，也写出晚春乡村的明亮色彩。
imagery.en: A sea of golden rape flowers hides the butterfly and fills the late-spring countryside with colour.
